## PureChain v1.0.0

First tagged release of the PureChain execution client.

### What this is

PureChain is a **permissioned, free-gas EVM network**. Transactions cost zero —
there is no base fee and no tip — and blocks are produced by a known set of
validators rather than by open mining or staking.

This client is a fork of **go-ethereum v1.13.15**, kept close to upstream so it
behaves like the geth operators already know: same CLI, same JSON-RPC, same
tooling. MetaMask, ethers.js, Hardhat and block explorers work unchanged. The
fork exists because PureChain needs a combination stock geth no longer
supports — a Proof-of-Authority (Clique) validator set running the current EVM
(Shanghai and Cancun: PUSH0, transient storage, EIP-4788) with zero-cost
transactions. Upstream ties post-Shanghai forks to the PoS Merge and dropped
Clique in v1.14, so this fork maintains that path.

### Download

| File | Platform |
|---|---|
| `purechain-geth-v1.0.0-linux-amd64` | Linux x86-64 |
| `purechain-geth-v1.0.0-linux-arm64` | Linux ARM64 (incl. AWS Graviton) |

Statically linked (`CGO_ENABLED=0`), so they run on Alpine and glibc images
alike with no libc dependency.

```bash
chmod +x purechain-geth-v1.0.0-linux-amd64
./purechain-geth-v1.0.0-linux-amd64 version
```

### What's in this release

**Security.** 31 fixes backported from go-ethereum v1.13.15 → v1.17.5. Four are
in cryptographic code reachable from the p2p port *before* authentication —
including a remotely triggerable panic via the RLPx handshake and missing point
validation on externally supplied public keys. Also adds bounds on pre-auth
handshake messages, JSON-RPC method names, log-filter addresses and fee-history
percentiles. The full adoption matrix, including what was rejected and why, is
in [`docs/upstream-backports.md`](docs/upstream-backports.md).

**Stability.** Crash and corruption fixes in the freezer, snapshot layers,
state copying, the transaction pools and the RPC layer; goroutine leaks closed
in `eth/filters` and the eth protocol dispatcher.

**Faster transaction inclusion.** The Clique out-of-turn sealing delay is now
drawn once per block and anchored to an absolute deadline, instead of being
redrawn on every re-seal. This makes `--miner.recommit` below the block period
safe on multi-signer chains, which roughly halves inclusion latency
(~2.0 s → ~1.0 s at a one-second block period).

**Testing.** `smoke-test/` covers Cancun opcodes, free-gas RPC, wallet and
ethers compatibility, snap sync, fork transitions and release-to-release
upgrades. `rehearsal/` is a six-node Docker harness for rehearsing a node
upgrade end to end — rolling upgrade under load, stress to saturation, outage
and crash drills, a signer-quorum halt drill, and rollback in both directions —
with a hard gate at every step.

### Running a node

[`docs/operator-guide.md`](docs/operator-guide.md) covers build, genesis and
signer setup; [`network/`](network/) generates a genesis for your own validator
set; [`docs/upgrade-runbook.md`](docs/upgrade-runbook.md) covers upgrading an
existing Clique chain in place.

Upgrading between builds of this client is cumulative — no genesis, config or
on-disk format change. Roll nodes one at a time, and downgrade the same way.
